VKF 0.1.4 — Standard Kernels And Numeric Lowering

VKF 0.1.4 replaces the previous ad-hoc language comparison with published, recognizable algorithms and improves the direct x64 backend where those kernels exposed avoidable work.

What changed from 0.1.3

  • The comparison suite now uses spectral norm, fannkuch-redux, and n-body, adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game at fixed small, medium, and large scales.
  • Exact VKF, C, Rust, Zig, Go, Julia, and Python sources are materialized and linked from the report. Numeric output must contain exactly one finite value; missing or duplicate output fails verification.
  • C, Rust, and Zig join VKF in raw in-process kernel timing. Fresh-process compile and runtime remain separate measurements.
  • Fixed-vector indexing records integer type evidence. Dominating constant bounds and canonical nonnegative induction remove only checks proven redundant; unproven and fractional indices retain runtime errors.
  • Long numeric expressions lower directly through x64 registers instead of spilling every intermediate stack value.
  • Proven fixed-vector indices remain in integer registers across adjacent hot expressions and updates.
  • Parameters in numeric-scalar functions become constants only when every direct call supplies the same literal and the parameter is not mutated or aliased by a fixed-vector update. Aggregate returns remain unchanged.
  • The scalar recurrence optimizer preserves branch behavior and numeric order.
  • Linux minimal numeric output writes exactly one result line.

Verification contract

Release publication requires all of the following from the tagged source:

  • 301 native VKF tests on Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64;
  • every documented program compiled 100 times and run 100 times on all three release targets with exact output and source/compiler hashes;
  • 100-run seven-language comparison on Linux x64;
  • direct compiler lowering with no Python, C++ compiler, assembler, linker, or compatibility fallback at user compile time or runtime.

The historical 20,000-operation scalar engineering gate remains under 10 ms mean compiler-core time and 500 microseconds mean raw runtime. Those limits do not apply to the larger standard kernels.

Interpretation

Results are evidence for the exact code, host, toolchains, and work counts in the report—not a claim that VKF is universally faster than another language. See benchmark policy for provenance and limits.

Native library scope remains math, stat, random, time, io, collections, errors, system, process, and regex. physics, ui, and symbolic remain excluded rather than shipping partial implementations.
